summary:
**Conversation Overview**

This conversation continued a long-running Phase R2 computational audit of a physics/mathematics reference work called "The Method 1.6," a multi-volume project comprising a main volume, register, and several compendia. The person is conducting a systematic line-by-line review of the main volume, re-measuring every general claim exhaustively using Python instruments run against a rebuilt mathematical structure (a lattice called Λ with tower stages Λ₈ through Λ₁₃). The session covered main volume sections §12.8–12.9, §12.10, and §12.11–12.11.0, producing READ files (deviation reports), CENSUS-CLOSURES files (tracking defect rows), and r2-ch12c/12d/12e.py instruments for each segment.

The work follows strict standing rulings: every stated value must be recomputed from files (never recited), claims must be labeled MEASURED/INFERRED/record-carried, no corrections or Register entries are made until the review closes, instruments travel as bundle members in versioned builds (BUILD90 main → BUILD98 compendia), and handoffs occur at 90–95% context with executable gate instructions. Chat 72 gated BUILD97 (PASS), produced nine new member files, appended W-108 to the Working Register, and produced BUILD98 (3,028,463 B, md5 e34f089ca1127301c33b72dd21d7d2fe, 175 members). Key findings of substance: the "⟨q⟩ → 1.887" figure printed as Λ₁₃'s endpoint is actually Λ₁₁'s mean (1.8874); §12.8.5's independence claim is logically false (E(Λ)=0 forces every fibre and projection closed); "most active constraint" reverses on the comparable-interval population; "all 1,654 targets are legal sources" fails for 485 cells with g=0; and a Q-list pointer in §12.10.2 points to a nonexistent Appendix E item.

The conversation concluded with HANDOFF-23 written for chat 73, directing continuation at §12.11.0.1 (L2577), with Drive upload instructions (upload HANDOFF-23 and BUILD98; retire HANDOFF-22 and BUILD97), files presented to outputs, and the full executable gate reproduced with updated byte counts, md5s, and instrument reproduction figures for all instruments through r2-ch12e.py.

**Tool Knowledge**

Google Drive searches used `title contains 'BUILD98_compendia' or title contains 'BUILD90_main'` with `pageSize 5` and `excludeContentSnippets True`; the `title contains` operator reliably locates bundles by build number even when filenames include long descriptive suffixes. Downloaded files spill to `/mnt/user-data/tool_results/<tool_call_id>.json` and must be decoded via `base64.b64decode(json.loads(json.load(open(p))[0]['text'])['content'], validate=True)` — hand-transcription of base64 is prohibited. When HANDOFF-21 was searched by exact title (`title = 'HANDOFF-21.md'`) and by contains, both returned nothing, confirming retired files are fully removed from Drive; the needed figures were recovered from a prior chat transcript instead. The `conversation_search` tool was used to search prior chat transcripts by conversation ID for specific technical figures (VARIANT line counts, constants), though in this session those searches returned no results and the figures were sourced from the uploaded handoff and chat-70 transcript instead.

1	---
     2	name: file-reading
     3	description: "Use this skill when a file has been uploaded but its content is NOT in your context — only its path at /mnt/user-data/uploads/ is listed in an uploaded_files block. This skill is a router: it tells you which tool to use for each file type (pdf, docx, xlsx, csv, json, images, archives, ebooks) so you read the right amount the right way instead of blindly running cat on a binary. Triggers: any mention of /mnt/user-data/uploads/, an uploaded_files section, a file_path tag, or a user asking about an uploaded file you have not yet read. Do NOT use this skill if the file content is already visible in your context inside a documents block — you already have it."
     4	compatibility: "claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cowork — any surface where uploads land at /mnt/user-data/uploads/"
     5	license: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms
     6	---
     7	
     8	# Reading Uploaded Files
     9	
    10	## Why this skill exists
    11	
    12	When a user uploads a file in claude.ai, Claude Desktop, or Cowork,
    13	the file is written to `/mnt/user-data/uploads/<filename>` and you are told the path
    14	in an `<uploaded_files>` block. **The content is not in your context.**
    15	You must go read it.
    16	
    17	The naive thing — `cat /mnt/user-data/uploads/whatever` — is wrong for
    18	most files:
    19	
    20	- On a PDF it prints binary garbage.
    21	- On a 100MB CSV it floods your context with rows you will never use.
    22	- On a DOCX it prints the raw ZIP bytes.
    23	- On an image it does nothing useful at all.
    24	
    25	This skill tells you the right first move for each type, and when to
    26	hand off to a deeper skill.
    27	
    28	## General protocol
    29	
    30	1. **Look at the extension.** That is your dispatch key.
    31	2. **Stat before you read.** Large files need sampling, not slurping.
    32	   ```bash
    33	   stat -c '%s bytes, %y' /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    34	   file /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    35	   ```
    36	3. **Read just enough to answer the user's question.** If they asked
    37	   "how many rows are in this CSV", don't load the whole thing into
    38	   pandas — `wc -l` gives a fast approximation (it counts newlines,
    39	   not CSV records, so it may over-count if quoted fields contain
    40	   embedded newlines).
    41	4. **If a dedicated skill exists, go read it.** The table below tells
    42	   you when. The dedicated skills cover editing, creating, and advanced
    43	   operations that this skill does not.
    44	
    45	## `extract-text`
    46	
    47	For docx, odt, epub, xlsx, pptx, rtf, and ipynb the first move is
    48	`extract-text <file>`. It emits markdown for docx/odt/epub (headings,
    49	bold, lists, links, tables), tab-separated rows under `## Sheet:`
    50	headers for xlsx, text under `## Slide N` headers for pptx, fenced
    51	code cells for ipynb, and plain text for rtf. Pass `--format <fmt>`
    52	when the extension is wrong or absent (e.g., `--format xlsx` on an
    53	`.xlsm`). If it errors on a file, `pandoc <file> -t plain` is a
    54	fallback; for xlsx/pptx, fall back to the dedicated skill's
    55	Python-based approach (openpyxl / python-pptx).
    56	
    57	## Dispatch table
    58	
    59	Where a dedicated skill is named below, invoke it by name if you have a
    60	Skill tool, or Read its SKILL.md (listed in your available skills, or in
    61	the same skills directory as this file).
    62	
    63	| Extension                         | First move                                           | Dedicated skill |
    64	| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
    65	| `.pdf`                            | Content inventory (see PDF section)                  | `pdf-reading`   |
    66	| `.docx`                           | `extract-text`                                       | `docx`          |
    67	| `.doc` (legacy)                   | Convert to `.docx` first                             | `docx`          |
    68	| `.xlsx`                           | `extract-text`                                       | `xlsx`          |
    69	| `.xlsm`                           | `extract-text --format xlsx`                         | `xlsx`          |
    70	| `.xls` (legacy)                   | `pd.read_excel(engine="xlrd")` — openpyxl rejects it | `xlsx`          |
    71	| `.ods`                            | `pd.read_excel(engine="odf")` — openpyxl rejects it  | `xlsx`          |
    72	| `.pptx`                           | `extract-text`                                       | `pptx`          |
    73	| `.ppt` (legacy)                   | Convert to `.pptx` first                             | `pptx`          |
    74	| `.csv`, `.tsv`                    | `pandas` with `nrows`                                | — (below)       |
    75	| `.json`, `.jsonl`                 | `jq` for structure                                   | — (below)       |
    76	| `.jpg`, `.png`, `.gif`, `.webp`   | Already in your context as vision input              | — (below)       |
    77	| `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`         | List contents, do **not** auto-extract               | — (below)       |
    78	| `.gz` (single file)               | `zcat \| head` — no manifest to list                 | — (below)       |
    79	| `.epub`, `.odt`                   | `extract-text`                                       | — (below)       |
    80	| `.rtf`                            | `extract-text`                                       | — (below)       |
    81	| `.ipynb`                          | `extract-text`                                       | — (below)       |
    82	| `.txt`, `.md`, `.log`, code files | `wc -c` then `head` or full `cat`                    | — (below)       |
    83	| Unknown                           | `file` then decide                                   | —               |
    84	
    85	---
    86	
    87	## PDF
    88	
    89	**Never** `cat` a PDF — it prints binary garbage.
    90	
    91	Quick first move — get the page count and determine whether the PDF
    92	has an extractable text layer:
    93	
    94	```bash
    95	pdfinfo /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    96	pdffonts /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    97	```
    98	
    99	`pdffonts` tells you whether text extraction will work before you try it:
   100	
   101	- **No fonts listed** (empty table, just the header) → the PDF is a
   102	  scan or raster export. `pdftotext` and `PdfReader.extract_text()`
   103	  will return nothing useful. Go straight to page rasterization or OCR
   104	  — see the `pdf-reading` skill → "Scanned documents".
   105	- **Fonts listed** → there is a text layer; extract it:
   106	  ```bash
   107	  pdftotext -f 1 -l 1 /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf - | head -20
   108	  ```
   109	
   110	The reason to check `pdffonts` first is user-facing: running
   111	`pdftotext` on a scan produces an empty result, and in a visible
   112	transcript that reads as a failed first attempt before you fall back
   113	to OCR. The two-line diagnostic above costs one tool call and avoids
   114	that — you arrive at the right method on the first try, which is what
   115	a user perceives as "it just read my file."
   116	
   117	That also shapes how to open your reply. The diagnostic commands are
   118	plumbing, not content; lead with what the user asked about. On a
   119	scanned receipt that might be "This is a 3-page scanned invoice; the
   120	amount due on page 2 is $1,845.00," and on a digitally-authored report
   121	it might be "The Q3 report runs 28 pages; revenue on p. 4 is $12.3M,
   122	up 9% YoY." What you're steering away from is the "I'll examine the
   123	PDF" / "Let me check if this is extractable" preamble — the answer to
   124	their question is the first thing they should see.
   125	
   126	For anything beyond a quick peek — figures, tables, attachments,
   127	forms, scanned PDFs, visual inspection, or choosing a reading strategy
   128	— go read the `pdf-reading` skill. It covers content inventory, text
   129	extraction vs. page rasterization, embedded content extraction, and
   130	document-type-aware reading strategies.
   131	
   132	For PDF form filling, creation, merging, splitting, or watermarking,
   133	go read the `pdf` skill.
   134	
   135	---
   136	
   137	## DOCX / DOC
   138	
   139	The `docx` skill covers editing, creating, tracked changes, images.
   140	Read it if you need any of those. For a quick look:
   141	
   142	```bash
   143	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/memo.docx | head -200
   144	```
   145	
   146	Legacy `.doc` (not `.docx`) must be converted first — see the `docx`
   147	skill.
   148	
   149	---
   150	
   151	## XLSX / XLS / spreadsheets
   152	
   153	The `xlsx` skill covers formulas, formatting, charts, creating. Read
   154	it if you need any of those. For a quick look at an `.xlsx`:
   155	
   156	```bash
   157	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.xlsx | head -100
   158	```
   159	
   160	For `.xlsm`, add `--format xlsx` (same zip structure; only the
   161	extension differs). When you need a structured preview in Python:
   162	
   163	```python
   164	from openpyxl import load_workbook
   165	wb = load_workbook("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.xlsx", read_only=True)
   166	print("Sheets:", wb.sheetnames)
   167	ws = wb.active
   168	for row in ws.iter_rows(max_row=5, values_only=True):
   169	    print(row)
   170	```
   171	
   172	`read_only=True` matters — without it, openpyxl loads the entire
   173	workbook into memory, which breaks on large files. Do not trust
   174	`ws.max_row` in read-only mode: many non-Excel writers omit the
   175	dimension record, so it comes back `None` or wrong. If you need a row
   176	count, iterate or use pandas.
   177	
   178	**Legacy `.xls`** — openpyxl raises `InvalidFileException`. Use:
   179	
   180	```python
   181	import pandas as pd
   182	df = pd.read_excel("/mnt/user-data/uploads/old.xls", engine="xlrd", nrows=5)
   183	```
   184	
   185	**`.ods` (OpenDocument)** — openpyxl also rejects this. Use:
   186	
   187	```python
   188	import pandas as pd
   189	df = pd.read_excel("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.ods", engine="odf", nrows=5)
   190	```
   191	
   192	---
   193	
   194	## PPTX
   195	
   196	```bash
   197	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/deck.pptx | head -200
   198	```
   199	
   200	**Legacy `.ppt`** — convert to `.pptx` first via LibreOffice; see the
   201	`pptx` skill for the sandbox-safe `scripts/office/soffice.py` wrapper
   202	(bare `soffice` hangs here because the seccomp filter blocks the
   203	`AF_UNIX` sockets LibreOffice uses for instance management).
   204	
   205	For anything beyond reading, go to the `pptx` skill.
   206	
   207	---
   208	
   209	## CSV / TSV
   210	
   211	**Do not** `cat` or `head` these blindly. A CSV with a 50KB quoted cell
   212	in row 1 will wreck your `head -5`. Use pandas with `nrows`:
   213	
   214	```python
   215	import pandas as pd
   216	df = pd.read_csv("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.csv", nrows=5)
   217	print(df)
   218	print()
   219	print(df.dtypes)
   220	```
   221	
   222	Approximate row count without loading (over-counts if the file has
   223	RFC-4180 quoted newlines — the same quoted-cell case this section
   224	warned about above):
   225	
   226	```bash
   227	wc -l /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.csv
   228	```
   229	
   230	Full analysis only after you know the shape:
   231	
   232	```python
   233	df = pd.read_csv("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.csv")
   234	print(df.describe())
   235	```
   236	
   237	TSV: same, with `sep="\t"`.
   238	
   239	---
   240	
   241	## JSON / JSONL
   242	
   243	Structure first, content second:
   244	
   245	```bash
   246	jq 'type' /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.json
   247	jq 'if type == "array" then length elif type == "object" then keys else . end' /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.json
   248	```
   249	
   250	(`keys` errors on scalar JSON roots — a bare `"hello"` or `42` is valid
   251	JSON per RFC 7159 — so guard the branch.)
   252	
   253	Then drill into what the user actually asked about.
   254	
   255	JSONL (one object per line) — do **not** `jq` the whole file; work line
   256	by line:
   257	
   258	```bash
   259	head -3 /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.jsonl | jq .
   260	wc -l /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.jsonl
   261	```
   262	
   263	---
   264	
   265	## Images (JPG / PNG / GIF / WEBP)
   266	
   267	**You can already see uploaded images.** They are injected into your
   268	context as vision inputs alongside the `<uploaded_files>` pointer. You
   269	do not need to read them from disk to describe them.
   270

 2432|  1.887 — coupling multiplicity re-weights the profile toward higher transfer, per §12.11.5.

{"returncode":0,"stdout":" 2451| 
 2452|       The shape is not a cylinder over an arbitrary set. It is a cylinder whose every
 2453|       cross-section satisfies this book's own law.
 2454| 
 2455| ### 12.8.5 Which gives E(X) a local form
 2456|       E(Λ) = 0 and E(A_q) = E(B_q) = 0 for every q.
 2457| 
 2458|  **The second does not follow from the first.** A closed index could in principle have defective slices that cancel in the total. **Here none do**, and that is a new invariant.
 2459| 
 2460| ### 12.9 Every other shape the lattice contains
 2461|  Intervals. \[x,y\] is a box iff no constraint binds across it:
 2462| 
 2463|       I_{x,y} = Box(x,y) ⟺ for every constraint i ≤ f(j), y_i ≤ f(x_j)
 2464| 
 2465|  **Exact on 60 of 60 tested**, and only **27%** of random intervals qualify — **the other 73% are where the physics is active.** The binding rates rank the constraints:
 2466| 
 2467|   constraint                                                            binds
 2468|   g≤q                                                                   35.6%
 2469|   q≤k                                                                   33.0%
 2470|   g ≤ 4f+2                                                              4.9%
 2471| 
 2472|  **The most active constraint is the coupling; the least is the Pauli bound — which is why §16.8 finds it the cheapest to violate.** Two independent measures, one answer.
 2473| 
 2474|  **Rank levels.** Eighteen antichains, the largest **122 at rank 11**: the biggest set of configurations no two of which can be reached from each other by adding electrons. **Λ is exactly eight times its widest level.**
 2475| 
 2476|  **Maximal chains.** A distributive lattice is J(P); **its maximal chains are the linear extensions of P.** With seventeen join-irreducibles and a chain length of seventeen:
 2477| 
 2478|     e(P) = 1,113,045,672
 2479| 
 2480|  **The seventeen generators of §8.3 and the chain length of seventeen are the same seventeen**, and the book reports both without connecting them.
 2481| 
 2482|  **And one shape absent.** No Möbius band, no cycle, no non-planar minor — **the constraint graph is a tree, so there is nothing to twist and nothing to close.** §12.1's finding follows by construction, not by search.
 2483| 
","stderr":""}

That the cylinder's two sides carry different trees — caterpillar against path, the pendant on one side only — with closed forms exact at every q, and that the fibration iterates in three levels to a floor of boxes, is this book's.**
1211| 
1212| ### Four numbers, five facts
1213| 
1214| **The counts 165, 330, 345, 136 carry more than their sum — five facts read off the table, every one verified exhaustively. First, a Pareto frontier inside the lattice: |A_q| falls 33, 33, 23, 8 while |B_q| rises 5, 10, 15, 17, so raising the transfer costs the parent and pays the target, monotonically, and no q improves both — the shape of §23.5's dw/dh > 0 with dV/dh < 0, which the book presents as a fact about brackets and is here a fact about the index itself. Second, a most-probable transfer: the fibre peaks at q = 2 with 345 cells, 35.3% of Λ, the sequence is log-concave hence unimodal, and the mean transfer ⟨q⟩ = 1428/976 = 1.4631, sd 0.930, is S′(1)/S(1) in the base variable — the number of electrons moved, averaged over every admissible configuration. Third, an 8-to-3 compression that loses no count: Λ's generating function has eight variables, the shape has three, and S(1,1,1) = 976 — not a projection that forgets cells but one that forgets which coordinate inside each side and keeps how many, a general fact about caterpillars, a path with one pendant reducing to (base, left, right) whatever its length. Fourth, every cross-section is itself a closed, modular lattice: all eight slices — A_q and B_q at each of the four q — are closed under coordinatewise join and meet with E = 0, and the modular law x ∨ (a ∧ b) = (x ∨ a) ∧ b for x ≤ b hold
1215| 
1216| *the fibre table of the two-body separation (§12.6.1); all five facts at the caps of §7.4, (n, e, ℓ, k, f) = (3, 3, 1, 3, 1); closure, the modular law and the distributive law checked on every triple of every slice; the mean exact as 1428/976.*
1217| 
1218| Proved — M §12.8; Pareto 1896; Laplace 1812; Dedekind 1900; Birkhoff 1937; Harary & Schwenk 1973; Stanley 1989.
1219| 
1220| > **Prior art: the frontier on which no move improves both objectives is Pareto, *Cours d'économie politique* (1896); the mean as G′(1)/G(1) of a generating function is Laplace, *Théorie analytique des probabilités* (1812); that a positive log-concave sequence is unimodal is elementary, surveyed in Stanley (1989); the modular law is Dedekind (1900); that a sublattice of a product of chains is distributive, hence modular, is Birkhoff (1937); the caterpillar reduction to (base, left, right) rests on Harary & Schwenk (1973). That the fibre table carries all five at once — a Pareto frontier inside an index, a most-probable transfer, a count-preserving compression, cross-sections every one closed and modular, and a local form of E — is this book's.**
1221| 
1222| ### Every other shape the lattice contains
1223| 
1224| **Intervals, antichains, chains — and one shape absent. An interval [x, y] is a box exactly when no constraint binds across it: I_{x,y} = Box(x, y) ⟺ for every constraint u ≤ φ(v), y_u ≤ φ(x_v) — the record tested sixty of sixty, and the criterion is here proved by exhaustion, agreeing with direct enumeration on all 115,162 comparable intervals without exception. Boxes are 31,604 of 115,162 — 27.4%, the record's sampled 27% now the exact population figure — and the other 72.6% are where the physics is active: some constraint binds. The binding rates rank the constraints — the record's sample reads g ≤ q at 35.6%, q ≤ k at 33.0%, g ≤ 4f + 2 at 4.9% (§12.9), and over the full population of meet-join intervals [x∧y, x∨y] of all 475,800 unordered pairs, exhaustively, the rates are 30.0%, 28.0% and 1.9% — the same order on both bases. The most active constraint is the coupling; the least is the Pauli bound — which §16.8 finds the cheapest to violate; two independent measures, one answer. The eighteen rank levels partition Λ into eighteen antichains while every maximal chain carries exactly eighteen cells, so the minimum antichain partition and the maximum chain meet at eighteen — Mirsky's dual of Dilworth, exactly attained; the largest level, 122 at rank 11, is the largest antichain outright, certified by the Dilworth chain partition of the Spern
1225| 
1226| *the interval census exhaustive over all 115,162 comparable intervals at the caps of §7.4, (n, e, ℓ, k, f) = (3, 3, 1, 3, 1); binding rates on two bases, the record's sample and the exhaustive meet-join population, each named; e(P) by independent chain-counting on the rank grading.*

input.file_text:
# r2-ch12c.py — Phase R2 instrument for main §12.8–§12.9 (chat 72). Requires tower-2.py beside it.
# Every figure printed here is measured on ALL cells, ALL comparable pairs or ALL 475,800 unordered pairs of the rebuilt Λ8,
# and on the rebuilt Λ9…Λ13 where the claim reaches the tower. Nothing is sampled.
import importlib.util, itertools, collections, math, random, sys
from fractions import Fraction
import numpy as np
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('tower','tower-2.py'); tw=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(tw)
L8=tw.L8(); n=len(L8); S8=set(L8); print('|Λ8| =',n)
NAMES='n l k q e f g 2S'.split()
X=np.array(L8,dtype=np.int16)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------- §12.8 the fibre table (two-body separation of §12.6.1)
Aof=lambda c:(c[0],c[1],c[2],c[7]); Bof=lambda c:(c[4],c[5],c[6])
N={}; Aq={}; Bq={}
for qq in range(4):
    C=[c for c in L8 if c[3]==qq]; N[qq]=len(C); Aq[qq]=set(map(Aof,C)); Bq[qq]=set(map(Bof,C))
A=[len(Aq[q]) for q in range(4)]; B=[len(Bq[q]) for q in range(4)]
print('§12.8 fibre counts N_q =',[N[q] for q in range(4)],'Σ =',sum(N.values()),'| |A_q| =',A,'| |B_q| =',B,'| |A_q||B_q| =',[A[q]*B[q] for q in range(4)],'exact separation at every q:',all(A[q]*B[q]==N[q] for q in range(4)))
print('§12.8.1 |A_q| non-increasing:',all(A[i]>=A[i+1] for i in range(3)),'| falls at EVERY step (strict):',all(A[i]>A[i+1] for i in range(3)),'| |B_q| rises at every step (strict):',all(B[i]<B[i+1] for i in range(3)))
print('  no q improves both (no ordered pair q≠q′ with |A_q|>|A_q′| and |B_q|>|B_q′|):',not any(A[i]>A[j] and B[i]>B[j] for i in range(4) for j in range(4) if i!=j))
# §12.8.2
seq=[N[q] for q in range(4)]; p=max(range(4),key=lambda q:seq[q])
mean=Fraction(sum(q*N[q] for q in range(4)),n); m2=Fraction(sum(q*q*N[q] for q in range(4)),n); var=m2-mean*mean
print('§12.8.2 peak at q=%d with %d cells = %.2f%% of Λ | log-concave (N_q² ≥ N_{q−1}N_{q+1} at q=1,2): %s | unimodal (rises to the peak, falls after): %s'%(p,seq[p],100*seq[p]/n,all(seq[i]**2>=seq[i-1]*seq[i+1] for i in (1,2)),all(seq[i]<=seq[i+1] for i in range(p)) and all(seq[i]>=seq[i+1] for i in range(p,3))))
print('  ⟨q⟩ = Σ q·N_q / 976 = %d/976 = %.4f | sd = %.4f'%(sum(q*N[q] for q in range(4)),float(mean),math.sqrt(float(var))))
# §12.8.3 the shape polynomial S(base,left,right) = Σ_q base^q · A_q(left) · B_q(right): S(1,1,1) and S′_base(1)/S(1)
S111=sum(A[q]*B[q] for q in range(4)); Sp=sum(q*A[q]*B[q] for q in range(4))
print('§12.8.3 S(1,1,1) = Σ_q |A_q||B_q| = %d | S′(1)/S(1) in the base variable = %d/%d = %.4f (equals ⟨q⟩ because the separation is exact at every q)'%(S111,Sp,S111,Sp/S111))
# §12.8.4 the eight slices: closure (E), the modular law on conditioned triples, the distributive law on all triples
def closure(Xs):
    Xs=set(Xs)
    while True:
        new=set()
        for a in Xs:
            for b in Xs:
                j=tuple(map(max,a,b)); m=tuple(map(min,a,b))
                if j not in Xs: new.add(j)
                if m not in Xs: new.add(m)
        if not new: return Xs
        Xs|=new
def leq(a,b): return all(u<=v for u,v in zip(a,b))
def jn(a,b): return tuple(map(max,a,b))
def mt(a,b): return tuple(map(min,a,b))
totE=0; modtrip=0; modtrip_strict=0; modfail=0; distrip=0; disfail=0; lattice_ok=True
for side,D in (('A',Aq),('B',Bq)):
    for qq in range(4):
        Xs=D[qq]; E=len(closure(Xs))-len(Xs); totE+=E
        el=list(Xs)
        for x in el:
            for b in el:
                if leq(x,b):
                    for a in el:
                        modtrip+=1; modtrip_strict+= (x!=b)
                        if jn(x,mt(a,b))!=mt(jn(x,a),b): modfail+=1
        for a in el:
            for b in el:
                for c in el:
                    distrip+=1
                    if mt(a,jn(b,c))!=jn(mt(a,b),mt(a,c)): disfail+=1
        print('  slice %s_%d: |X| = %2d  E(X) = %d  closed under coordinatewise join and meet: %s'%(side,qq,len(Xs),E,E==0))
print('§12.8.4 all eight slices closed (ΣE = %d) | modular law x∨(a∧b) = (x∨a)∧b for x ≤ b: %d conditioned triples (x ≤ b incl. x = b), %d with x < b, failures %d | distributive law a∧(b∨c) = (a∧b)∨(a∧c): %d ordered triples, failures %d'%(totE,modtrip,modtrip_strict,modfail,distrip,disfail))
# §12.8.5 "the second does not follow from the first": E(Λ)=0 ⇒ every fixed-q fibre and its two projections are closed.
#   Proof. x,y ∈ A_q lift to cells (x,q,b),(y,q,b′) ∈ Λ; Λ closed ⇒ (x∨y, q, b∨b′) ∈ Λ (max(q,q)=q) ⇒ x∨y ∈ A_q; likewise meets and B_q.
#   Mechanical corroboration on random closed sets: no closed set in a small box has a defective slice.
rng=random.Random(1); trials=0; fails=0
for t in range(3000):
    d=rng.choice([3,4]); box=list(itertools.product(range(3),repeat=d))
    Xs=closure(set(rng.sample(box,rng.randint(2,8)))); trials+=1
    for i in range(d):
        for v in range(3):
            fib=[c for c in Xs if c[i]==v]
            if not fib: continue

{"returncode":0,"stdout":"# READ-ch10 — Phase R2, main volume Chapter 10 "The void" (chat 71)

Member The_Method_1_6-2.md (BUILD90 main, md5 4aef772b…), L2021–L2074 (54 lines), read in full against (i) each cited section and Register entry, (ii) the rebuilt tower (tower-2.py, c0bce27a…), (iii) the chapter instrument r2-ch10.py (beside tower-2.py; every general claim measured on all 475,800 unordered pairs) and r2-tools.py. Rulings applied as in READ-ch7. Census rows in range: none; CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch10.tsv is the header alone.

## A. Deviations (both texts)

**10-01 · L2027–2028 (§10.1) — "exactly" names six of the seven constraints.** PRINTED: `The excluded cells are exactly those forbidden by Pauli (k > 2(2ℓ+1), g > cap), by the hydrogenic bound (ℓ ≥ n, f ≥ e), or by counting (q > k, g > q).` SOURCE: §7.1's seven constraints include 2S ≤ k (tower-2.py L8). MEASURED (r2-ch10.py, all 475,800 pairs; box points counted by the §10.4 closed form with and without the 2S ≤ k leaf, the closed form itself verified against brute force on every pair): of 23,242,166 void points, **1,885,246 (8.11 %) on 93,000 pairs pass all six printed co

**10-02 · L2033 against L2053–2054 and Appendix C L10255 — the range of the population is stated two ways.** PRINTED L2033: `across 776 million pairs and a seventeenfold range in cell count`; Figure 10.1 caption L2053: `across a hundredfold range in cell count, computed exhaustively over 776 million pairs`; App. C L10255: `2.4 points over a 100×`. SOURCE: the Register has no entry for this measurement (grep 'void-free', '776 million', '30.13', '20.19', '1.49': none); MC "The void-free fraction" (L1664–1666) carries it as "the measurement at the original larger population … which the 

**10-03 · L2033, L2049, L2053–2054 — the 776-million-pair figures cannot be recomputed.** PRINTED: `27.7–30.1%`; `Satisfied individually 67–94%; their product is 20.19%; the joint figure is 30.13% — a factor of 1.49 above independence, over the same 776 million pairs`. MEASURED at the base caps (3,3,1,3,1), all 475,800 pairs (r2-ch10.py): void-free 134,871 = **28.35 %** (inside 27.7–30.1); individual rates **69.95–98.06 %** (ℓ ≤ n−1 84.46, k ≤ 2(2ℓ+1) 71.55, q ≤ k 71.97, 2S ≤ k 80.45, g ≤ q 69.95, f ≤ e−1 83.86, g ≤ 2(2f+1) 98.06), product **20.13 %**, join

**10-04 · L2049 last sentence, against MC "The void-free fraction" L1664.** PRINTED: `The correlation is not a coincidence: all seven constraints descend from two origins.` SOURCE (MC, Proved): the dependence is positive because constraints sharing a coordinate are two decreasing functions of that coordinate's width (Chebyshev), "and it is positive for this reason and no other"; conditioned on the shared interval the lift is 1.0000 in every stratum. READING: the chapter gives a different reason (shared origin) from the one its compendium proves (shared coordinates along the tree); §10.1 also

**10-05 · L2073 (closing sentence).** PRINTED: `An index whose constraint graph is a tree has its void in closed form; one with cycles does not.` SOURCE: A.10 (L9998) proves the tree direction only ("If the constraint graph … is a tree, the count … factorises with no inclusion–exclusion"). READING: the converse is asserted, not proved, and is false as a universal (a cycle forces a sieve in general, not the absence of any closed form). Overgeneralisation; lower. For R3: "one with cycles needs a sieve" or "is not guaranteed one".

**10-06 · layout.** L2024, L2030, L2063–2064, L2068–2069 four-space lines render as code (r2-tools.py layout); L2030's aphorism is set as code. Production.

## B. Verified (all MEASURED unless marked)

- L2024 void(x,y) = ∏(|Δᵢ|+1) − |[x∧y, x∨y] ∩ Λ|: Σ box points 48,928,521, Σ void 23,242,166 over all pairs; void-free 134,871 pairs (28.35 %), void-bearing 340,929 — agrees with r2-ch9's count.
- L2027–2028 the three named sources are §7.1's constraints (ℓ ≤ n−1, f ≤ e−1; k ≤ 2(2ℓ+1), g ≤ 2(2f+1); q ≤ k, g ≤ q): true of six (see 10-01 for the seventh). "g > cap" leaves the cap (2(2f+1)) to §7.4 — incidental.
- L2040 §12.11.0 (L2535) and L2045 §13.2 (L3640) resolve to their headings; "Λ₉ has both a predecessor and a successor" record-carried to Chapter 12.
- L2042–2046 with k ≥ 0 the rebuild has 1,001 cells; the 25 with k = 0 all have 2S = q = g = 0 ("forced to zero", "twenty-five cells"): true. Excluding them: 976; bounding box 6,912 (9,216 with k = 0): true, and the box is a second, independent count.
- L2047 Register 301 (R L1127): "the construction is short an eighth condition — (3,3,2,3) gives 1,548, and only (3,3,1,3) with k ≥ 1 gives 976": 1,548 reproduces at caps (n,e,ℓ,k) = (3,3,2,3) with no f-cap (f ≤ e−1 only) and 976 at (3,3,1,3) with f ≤ 1 and k ≥ 1 — consistent with 7-01 (976 needs the f-cap that §7.4 does not print). The paraphrase "seven constraints and nothing else … needed eight things" is fair to the entry.
- L2057–2058 §10.3 "iff hiᵢ ≤ φ(loⱼ) for each of the seven constraints": (all seven comparisons hold) ⇔ (void = 0) on all 475,800 pairs, 0 disagreements (printed: 3,168 pairs). O(1): seven comparisons per pair — INFERRED, immediate.
- L2061–2071 §10.4 closed form with the two leaf counts: equal to the brute-force |box ∩ Λ| on all 475,800 pairs, 0 mismatches (printed: eight random intervals). A.10 (L9998) is its proof home; the chapter does not point to it and A.10 does not point back — incidental (Appendix segment).
- L2073 "No Möbius function. No 2⁷-term inclusion–exclusion": follows from A.10 for the tree case — INFERRED.

SOURCE: no Register entry carries ⟨q⟩ at any stage (grep '1.887' → Register L4725 only, entry 1263, a quantum defect δ = 1.887; grep '⟨q⟩', '1.463', '1428' → none). MEASURED (r2-ch12c.py, every cell of every stage): ⟨q⟩ = 1428/976 = 1.4631 at Λ₈; 2787/1654 = 1.6850 at Λ₉; 4640/2535 = 1.8304 at Λ₁₀; **25,640/13,585 = 1.8874 at Λ₁₁**; 135,720/70,905 = 1.9141 at Λ₁₂; **381,520/199,130 = 1.9159 at Λ₁₃** — the printed Λ₁₃ sections themselves give 1.916, not 1.887. READING: the caption's figure is drawn at Λ₁₃ and the sentence pairs 1.887 with it; §12.11.5 names Λ₁₃ as the last stage and then gives Λ₁₁'s mean as the rise. A wrong-stage figure at two sites (L3466 is the §12.11.5 segment's; recorded here, settled there). Substance.

**12c-02 · L2458 (§12.8.5), and MC L1214 — "the second does not follow from the first" is false; the fifth fact is a corollary, not a new invariant.** PRINTED L2456–2458: `E(Λ) = 0 and E(A_q) = E(B_q) = 0 for every q. Here none do, and that is a new invariant.` MC L1214: `the second does not follow from the first — a closed index could in principle carry defective slices, and here none do, a new invariant.` SOURCE: E(X) = |ℛ(X)| − |X| (main L3), the defect of closure under coordinatewise join and meet — non-negative, so nothing can "cancel in the total". DERIVATION (two lines): x, y ∈ A_q lift to cells (x, q, b), (y, q, b′) ∈ Λ; E(Λ) = 0 gives (x ∨ y, q, b ∨ b′) ∈ Λ since max(q, q) = q; hence x ∨ y ∈ A_q, and likewise meets and B_q. So E(Λ) = 0 implies E(A_q) = E(B_q) = 0 for every q — every fixed-coordinate fibre of a closed set, and every coordinate projection of one, is closed. MEASURED (r2-ch12c.py): E = 0 on all eight slices (as printed); on 3,000 random closed subsets of [0,2]³ and [0,2]⁴, 0 fixed-coordinate fibres or projections with E > 0. READING: the printed independence claim is a logical error of the same class as 11-01 and 11-02 (a general statement false in general); the eight E = 0 values are true and follow from §7.3. On all 475,800 meet-join intervals: ℓ≤n−1 15.5 %, k≤2(2ℓ+1) 28.4 %, q≤k 28.0 %, 2S≤k 19.5 %, **g≤q 30.0 %**, f≤e−1 16.1 %, g≤4f+2 1.9 %: g ≤ q leads, and the MC's three figures reproduce exactly. READING: "most active" holds on the record's sample and on the meet-join population, and fails on the comparable-interval population by 34.1 against 32.6; the MC's "the same order on both bases" is true of the two bases it names and silent on the third, which is the base of its own box count. The printed table shows three of seven constraints; the other four sampled rates are unrecoverable — the exhaustive seven are above.

**12c-04 · L2472 against §7.1 L1759–1760 — "the coupling" names g ≤ q here and 2S ≤ k in the book's own taxonomy.** PRINTED L2472: `The most active constraint is the coupling` (g ≤ q, per the table above it). MEASURED (grep 'coupling' with 'g ≤' / 'constraint'): the first site that attaches "coupling" to g ≤ q is L2472 itself; Chapter 13 L3662 repeats it (`g ≤ q is the most active constraint — it is the coupling itself`); L2609 uses the taxonomy the other way (`a counting phenomenon, not a coupling one`). READING: the same sentence uses "the Pauli bound" in §7.1's origin taxonomy, under which "the coupling" is 2S ≤ k (24.9 % / 19.5 %, fourth of seven on both populations). If the intended sense is the edge that couples the two sides of the cylinder (k–q–g), it is nowhere defined before use. Wording, but it fixes the referent of a load-bearing sentence; lower. Chapter 13's L3662 is that segment's.

**12c-05 · §12.8–§12.9 whole — no Register entry for any figure in the segment.** PRINTED: ⟨q⟩ = 1428/976 = 1.4631, sd 0.930, 35.3 %, log-concavity, S(1,1,1) = 976, the eight slices closed and modular, `Exact on 60 of 60 tested`, `27%`, the binding rates, eighteen antichains, `122 at rank 11`, `exactly eight times`, `e(P) = 1,113,045,672`; MC adds 31,519 conditioned triples, 93,966 triples, 31,604 of 115,162 = 27.4 %, 30.0 / 28.0 / 1.9 %, `e(P) … recomputed independently this build`. Both MC entries cite `Proved — M §12.8` / `M §12.9` and prior art, and no Register entry. READING: the class of 10-02 and 12a-01 (printed measurements with no Register entry), here covering two whole sections and their two MC entries; the sample figures (60 of 60, 27 %, 35.6/33.0/4.9) have no recorded population. Every value is now MEASURED in r2-ch12c.py (§B); whether the Register receives entries is M's. Provenance. The MC's `recomputed independently this build` is a build remark in a reader-facing volume (Ruling 45 class; noted, not a concern).

**12c-06 · L2465 against MC L1224 — the main prints the sample where its compendium holds the population.** PRINTED L2465: `Exact on 60 of 60 tested, and only 27% of random intervals qualify — the other 73% are where the physics is active.` MC: `the criterion is here proved by exhaustion, agreeing with direct enumeration on all 115,162 comparable intervals without exception. Boxes are 31,604 of 115,162 — 27.4% … the other 72.6%`. MEASURED (r2-ch12c.py): agreement on 115,162 of 115,162; boxes 31,604 = 27.44 %; not boxes 72.56 %. **12c-01 · Figure 12.3 caption L2431–2432, and §12.11.5 L3466 — "1.887" is Λ₁₁'s mean transfer, printed as the tower's endpoint.** PRINTED L2430–2432: `The Pareto frontier on a log axis, Λ₁₃ solid against Λ₈ dotted … the tower shifts ⟨q⟩ from 1.463 to 1.887 — coupling multiplicity re-weights the profile toward higher transfer, per §12.11.5.` §12.11.5 L3463–3466: `sections 815 · 3,260 · 6,150 · 3,360 at Λ₁₁, 11,470 · 45,880 · 89,700 · 52,080 at Λ₁₃ … The mean transfer rises, ⟨q⟩ = 1.4631 → 1.887`. SOURCE: no Register entry carries ⟨q⟩ at any stage (grep '1.887' → Register L4725 only, entry 1263, a quantum defect δ = 1.887; grep '⟨q⟩', '1.463', '1428' → none). MEASURED (r2-ch12c.py, every cell of every stage): ⟨q⟩ = 1428/976 = 1.4631 at Λ₈; 2787/1654 = 1.6850 at Λ₉; 4640/2535 = 1.8304 at Λ₁₀; **25,640/13,585 = 1.8874 at Λ₁₁**; 135,720/70,905 = 1.9141 at Λ₁₂; **381,520/199,130 = 1.9159 at Λ₁₃** — the printed Λ₁₃ sections themselves give 1.916, not 1.887. READING: the caption's figure is drawn at Λ₁₃ and the sentence pairs 1.887 with it; §12.11.5 names Λ₁₃ as the last stage and then gives Λ₁₁'s mean as the rise. A wrong-stage figure at two sites (L3466 is the §12.11.5 segment's; recorded here, settled there). Substance.

**12c-02 · L2458 (§12.8.5), and MC L1214 — "the second does not follow from the first" is false; the fifth fact is a corollary, not a new invariant.** PRINTED L2456–2458: `E(Λ) = 0 and E(A_q) = E(B_q) = 0 for every q. The second does not follow from the first. A closed index could in principle have defective slices that cancel in the total. Here none do, and that is a new invariant.` MC L1214: `the second does not follow from the first — a closed index could in principle carry defective slices, and here none do, a new invariant.` SOURCE: E(X) = |ℛ(X)| − |X| (main L3), the defect of closure under coordinatewise join and meet — non-negative, so nothing can "cancel in the total". DERIVATION (two lines): x, y ∈ A_q lift to cells (x, q, b), (y, q, b′) ∈ Λ; E(Λ) = 0 gives (x ∨ y, q, b ∨ b′) ∈ Λ since max(q, q) = q; hence x ∨ y ∈ A_q, and likewise meets and B_q. So E(Λ) = 0 implies E(A_q) = E(B_q) = 0 for every q — every fixed-coordinate fibre of a closed set, and every coordinate projection of one, is closed. MEASURED (r2-ch12c.py): E = 0 on all eight slices (as printed); on 3,000 random closed subsets of [0,2]³ and [0,2]⁴, 0 fixed-coordinate fibres or projections with E > 0. READING: the printed independence claim is a logical error of the same class as 11-01 and 11-02 (a general statement false in general); the eight E = 0 values are true and follow from §7.3. Substance. For R3: "and the second follows from the first (closure passes to every fibre and projection)".

**12c-03 · L2472 (§12.9) — "the most active constraint" depends on the population, and on the population §12.9 defines it is q ≤ k, not g ≤ q.** PRINTED L2465–2472: `only 27% of random intervals qualify … The binding rates rank the constraints: g≤q 35.6% · q≤k 33.0% · g ≤ 4f+2 4.9% … The most active constraint is the coupling; the least is the Pauli bound`. MC L1224: `over the full population of meet-join intervals [x∧y, x∨y] of all 475,800 unordered pairs, exhaustively, the rates are 30.0%, 28.0% and 1.9% — the same order on both bases.` SOURCE: no Register entry for the sample (grep '35.6', 'binds', 'binding', 'random interval', 'of 60', 'Box(', 'I_{x,y}' → none), so "the record's sample" (MC) points at nothing and its population is unrecoverable. MEASURED (r2-ch12c.py): on **all 115,162 comparable intervals [x, y]** — the population the section is about and the one the MC's own 31,604 / 27.4 % is measured on — the rates are ℓ≤n−1 17.3 %, k≤2(2ℓ+1) 30.6 %, **q≤k 34.1 %**, 2S≤k 24.9 %, **g≤q 32.6 %**, f≤e−1 15.0 %, g≤4f+2 3.8 %: q ≤ k leads. On all 475,800 meet-join intervals: ℓ≤n−1 15.5 %, k≤2(2ℓ+1) 28.4 %, q≤k 28.0 %, 2S≤k 19.5 %, **g≤q 30.0 %**, f≤e−1 16.1 %, g≤4f+2 1.9 %: g ≤ q leads, and the MC's three figures reproduce exactly. READING: "most active" holds on the record's sample and on the meet-join population, and fails on the comparable-interval population by 34.1 against 32.6; the MC's "the same order on both bases" is true of the two bases it names and silent on the third, which is the base of its own box count. "The least is the Pauli bound" holds on both populations (g ≤ 4f+2; the other Pauli bound k ≤ 2(2ℓ+1) is second or third) — §16.8 L4710 names g ≤ 4f+2 explicitly, §12.9 does not. Substance (true of the sample, false on the whole population; class of 9-01, 9-02, 11-01). The printed table shows three of seven constraints; the other four sampled rates are unrecoverable — the exhaustive seven are above.

**12c-04 · L2472 against §7.1 L1759–1760 — "the coupling" names g ≤ q here and 2S ≤ k in the book's own taxonomy.** PRINTED L2472: `The most active constraint is the coupling` (g ≤ q, per the table above it). SOURCE §7.1 table L1756–1760: `g≤q — counting — cannot place more than were removed`; `2S ≤ k — vector coupling`; L1762 `four origins … Pauli, the hydrogenic radial solution, counting, or angular-momentum coupling`. MEASURED (grep 'coupling' with 'g ≤' / 'constraint'): the first site that attaches "coupling" to g ≤ q is L2472 itself; Chapter 13 L3662 repeats it (`g ≤ q is the most active constraint — it is the coupling itself`); L2609 uses the taxonomy the other way (`a counting phenomenon, not a coupling one`). READING: the same sentence uses "the Pauli bound" in §7.1's origin taxonomy, under which "the coupling" is 2S ≤ k (24.9 % / 19.5 %, fourth of seven on both populations). If the intended sense is the edge that couples the two sides of the cylinder (k–q–g), it is nowhere defined before use. Wording, but it fixes the referent of a load-bearing sentence; lower. Chapter 13's L3662 is that segment's.

**12c-05 · §12.8–§12.9 whole — no Register entry for any figure in the segment.** PRINTED: ⟨q⟩ = 1428/976 = 1.4631, sd 0.930, 35.3 %, log-concavity, S(1,1,1) = 976, the eight slices closed and modular, `Exact on 60 of 60 tested`, `27%`, the binding rates, eighteen antichains, `122 at rank 11`, `exactly eight times`, `e(P) = 1,113,045,672`; MC adds 31,519 conditioned triples, 93,966 triples, 31,604 of 115,162 = 27.4 %, 30.0 / 28.0 / 1.9 %, `e(P) … recomputed independently this build`. SOURCE: Register greps for '§12.8', '§12.9', 'Pareto', 'log-concave', 'Mirsky', 'Möbius', '1,113', '113,045', 'e(P)', 'maximal chain', '31,604', '31,519', '93,966', '27.4', '30.0%', '35.6', '60 of 60', 'sixty', 'Box(', '⟨q⟩', '1428' → none; 'unimodal' → entry 47 (an earlier 28-rank object, maximum 15 at rank 11, not Λ₈'s 18 levels); 'Sperner' → 44, 78, 1228 (the generator's L.sperner check, no figure); 'eight times' → 1466 (unrelated); 'linear extension' → 377, 380 (the 4,140 of Chapter 4). Both MC entries cite `Proved — M §12.8` / `M §12.9` and prior art, and no Register entry. READING: the class of 10-02 and 12a-01 (printed measurements with no Register entry), here covering two whole sections and their two MC entries; the sample figures (60 of 60, 27 %, 35.6/33.0/4.9) have no recorded population. Every value is now MEASURED in r2-ch12c.py (§B); whether the Register receives entries is M's. Provenance. The MC's `recomputed independently this build` is a build remark in a reader-facing volume (Ruling 45 class; noted, not a concern).

**12c-06 · L2465 against MC L1224 — the main prints the sample where its compendium holds the population.** PRINTED L2465: `Exact on 60 of 60 tested, and only 27% of random intervals qualify — the other 73% are where the physics is active.` MC: `the criterion is here proved by exhaustion, agreeing with direct enumeration on all 115,162 comparable intervals without exception. Boxes are 31,604 of 115,162 — 27.4% … the other 72.6%`. MEASURED (r2-ch12c.py): agreement on 115,162 of 115,162; boxes 31,604 = 27.44 %; not boxes 72.56 %. READING: no contradiction (27 %, 73 % are the rounded population figures); the main states a sample and calls its rates "the binding rates" without saying they are sampled. Lower; for R3 the main can carry the exhaustive figures its MC entry already has.

**12c-07 · L2424, L2426, caption L2430–2431 — "falls" is flat at the first step at both scales.** PRINTED: `|A_q| falls 33, 33, 23, 8`; `costs the parent … monotonically`; caption `A falls and B rises at both scales`. MEASURED: |A_q| = 33, 33, 23, 8 is non-increasing and not strictly falling (33 = 33 at q = 0 → 1); at Λ₁₃, |A(q)| = 2,294, 2,294, 1,794, 744 likewise; |B_q| = 5, 10, 15, 17 and 5, 20, 50, 70 rise strictly. "No q improves both" holds (no ordered pair q ≠ q′ with both |A| and |B| larger). Wording; lower.

**12c-08 · Figure 12.2 caption L2389 (previous segment, deferred here) — "every section is itself closed, per §12.8.4" cites a Λ₈ result for Λ₁₃'s sections.** PRINTED L2387–2389: `The sections read 2,294 × 5, 2,294 × 20, 1,794 × 50, 744 × 70 … Every section is itself closed, per §12.8.4`. SOURCE §12.8.4 L2446–2450: the table's rows are `q 0–3 · A and B, all eight` — Λ₈'s eight slices; MC L1216 scope: `all five facts at the caps of §7.4`. MEASURED (r2-ch12c.py): E = 0 on all four Λ₁₃ A-sections (2,294 · 2,294 · 1,794 · 744 elements) and all four B-sections (5 · 20 · 50 · 70) — the caption's claim is true; and it follows for every stage from the construction (every tower bound is a monotone two-coordinate or box bound, closed under coordinatewise max and min). READING: true claim, pointer to a narrower result; lower. HANDOFF-22's deferred item closes on this measurement.

**12c-09 · layout.** L2424, L2438–2439, L2452–2453, L2456, L2463, L2478 four-space lines render as code (r2-tools.py layout); the aphorism at L2452–2453 and the four displayed results are set as code. Production.

## B. Verified (all MEASURED unless marked)

- L2421, L2424 fibre counts N_q = 165, 330, 345, 136, Σ 976; |A_q| = 33, 33, 23, 8; |B_q| = 5, 10, 15, 17; |A_q||B_q| = N_q at every q (exact separation, §12.6.1 L2359 resolves).
- L2426 Pareto: no ordered pair q ≠ q′ improves both sides. §23.5 (L6272) resolves to its heading and its claim (L6290: `dw/dh > 0 and dV/dh < 0, for every monotone convex y and every h`).
- L2435–2439 peak q = 2, 345 cells = 35.35 % (printed 35.3 %); N_q² ≥ N_{q−1}N_{q+1} at q = 1, 2 (log-concave), unimodal; ⟨q⟩ = 1428/976 = 1.4631; sd 0.9303 (printed 0.930). S′(1)/S(1) in the base variable = 1428/976 — equal to ⟨q⟩ because the separation is exact at every q (INFERRED from the identity, then MEASURED as the same sum).
- L2442 S(1,1,1) = Σ_q |A_q||B_q| = 976; "eight variables" is Chapter 11's F (r2-ch11); "three" is (base q, left A, right B) — the base is the cut vertex q of the path n–ℓ–k–q–g–f–e, the pendant 2S hangs at k on the A side (r2-ch11, r2-ch12b): the reduction needs only that q separates the tree into two components; "a path with one pendant" is the shape Λ has, not the general condition — record-carried from 12b-02.
- L2448–2450 all eight slices E = 0; modular law x ∨ (a ∧ b) = (x ∨ a) ∧ b on 31,519 conditioned triples with x ≤ b (28,109 with x < b), 0 failures — MC's 31,519 exactly; distributive law a ∧ (b ∨ c) = (a ∧ b) ∨ (a ∧ c) on 93,966 ordered triples (Σ|X|³), 0 failures — MC's 93,966 exactly; §7.3 (L1776 "Λ is closed") resolves.
- L2456 E(Λ₈) = 0 (closure of all 976 cells; minmax.py agrees).
- L2461–2463 the box criterion: (I_{x,y} = Box(x,y)) ⟺ (y_i ≤ φ(x_j) for all seven constraints) on all 115,162 comparable pairs, 0 disagreements — the tree argument of A.10 restricted to intervals (upper corner against lower corner, φ monotone) — INFERRED as proof, MEASURED as population.
- L2465 boxes 31,604 of 115,162 = 27.44 % (printed 27 %; MC 27.4 %); on the meet-join population 134,871 of 475,800 = 28.35 %, agreeing with r2-ch9 and r2-ch10.
- L2468–2470 the MC's exhaustive meet-join rates g ≤ q 30.0 %, q ≤ k 28.0 %, g ≤ 4f+2 1.9 % reproduce to the printed decimal; the sample's 35.6 / 33.0 / 4.9 cannot be re-measured (no population; 12c-03, 12c-05).
- L2472 §16.8 (L4659) resolves to its heading and its claim at L4710 (`g ≤ 4f+2, the only constraint sharing its variable with a stricter one, is an order of magnitude cheaper to violate than any other`); "cheapest" is the chapter's word for "an order of magnitude cheaper than any other" — consistent.
- L2474 rank = coordinate sum; ranks 3..20 = 18 levels; every cover raises rank by exactly 1 (graded, 3,749 covers); level sizes 1, 5, 15, 34, 59, 87, 108, 121, 122, 115, 100, 79, 57, 37, 21, 10, 4, 1 (r2-ch11's F(z) coefficients); largest 122 at rank 11; 976 = 8 × 122; width(Λ₈) = 122 by Dilworth (n − maximum matching in the comparability bipartite graph) = the largest level (Sperner); §8.4 (L1873 "Sperner, and not symmetric") resolves. "Reached from each other by adding electrons" glosses the componentwise order, which also moves n, ℓ, e, f — incidental.
- L2476–2478 unique 0̂ = (1,0,1,0,1,0,0,0) and 1̂ = (3,1,3,3,3,1,3,3); every maximal chain 0̂ → 1̂ has exactly 17 steps = 18 cells (MC: "every maximal chain carries exactly eighteen cells"; Mirsky's 18 = 18); the number of maximal chains, by rank-graded path counting on the cover graph, **e(P) = 1,113,045,672** — reproduces exactly; join-irreducibles (exactly one lower cover) 17 = chain length 17 (Birkhoff; L2480 "the same seventeen" true); §8.3 (L1847 "Seventeen generators") resolves.
- L2482 constraint graph 8 vertices, 7 edges, connected — a tree; §12.1 (L2306) resolves; "follows by construction" is the tree argument — INFERRED, immediate.
- Caption L2431 Λ₁₃ sections 11,470 · 45,880 · 89,700 · 52,080 peak at q = 2 with 89,700 (L3464 the same); Λ₁₁'s printed 815 · 3,260 · 6,150 · 3,360 (L3463) reproduce; all six stages' sections in r2-ch12c.py.

## C. Incidental

- The MC entry's prior-art chain (Pareto 1896; Laplace 1812; Dedekind 1900; Birkhoff 1937; Harary & Schwenk 1973; Stanley 1989; Brightwell & Winkler 1991; Sperner 1928; Dilworth 1950; Mirsky 1971; Listing 1861; Möbius 1865; Kuratowski 1930; Wagner 1937; Freuder 1982) is read in the MC segment, not here; only the entries' figures were reproduced.

# r2-ch12d.py — Phase R2 instrument for main §12.10–§12.10.2 (chat 72). Requires tower-2.py beside it.
# The §12.10.1 table's Λ9 column, every row measured on ALL 1,654 cells and ALL C(1654,2) pairs (the print sampled 200,000).
import importlib.util, collections, math
import numpy as np
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('tower','tower-2.py'); tw=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(tw)
L8=tw.L8(); L9=tw.L9(); X8=np.array(L8,dtype=np.int16); X9=np.array(L9,dtype=np.int16)
print('|Λ8| =',len(L8),'| |Λ9| =',len(L9),'(2S′ ∈ [0, g] adjoined to every cell)')
for name,X in (('Λ8',X8),('Λ9',X9)):
    n=len(X); lo=X.min(axis=0); hi=X.max(axis=0); box=int(np.prod(hi-lo+1))
    # closure defect E = |ℛ(X)| − |X| under coordinatewise join and meet, all n² ordered pairs
    S=set(map(tuple,X.tolist())); J=np.maximum(X[:,None,:],X[None,:,:]).reshape(-1,X.shape[1]); M=np.minimum(X[:,None,:],X[None,:,:]).reshape(-1,X.shape[1])
    E=len(set(map(tuple,J.tolist()))|set(map(tuple,M.tolist()))|S)-n
    rank=X.sum(axis=1).astype(np.int64); levels=collections.Counter(rank.tolist()); lv=sorted(levels); seq=[levels[r] for r in lv]
    iu,ju=np.triu_indices(n,1)
    rj=np.maximum(X[iu],X[ju]).sum(axis=1).astype(np.int64); rm=np.minimum(X[iu],X[ju]).sum(axis=1).astype(np.int64)
    viol=int((rank[iu]+rank[ju]!=rj+rm).sum())
    Fm1=int(((-1)**rank).sum()); mx=max(seq); pk=[r for r in lv if levels[r]==mx]
    logc=all(seq[i]**2>=seq[i-1]*seq[i+1] for i in range(1,len(seq)-1)); p=seq.index(mx)
    unim=all(seq[i]<=seq[i+1] for i in range(p)) and all(seq[i]>=seq[i+1] for i in range(p,len(seq)-1))
    print('%s: cells %d | box ∏(hi−lo+1) = %d | E(X) = %d (sublattice of the box: %s) | rank-modular r(x)+r(y) = r(x∨y)+r(x∧y) on %d unordered pairs: violations %d | F(1) = %d | F(−1) = Σ(−1)^rank = %d | rank levels %d (ranks %d..%d), widest %d at rank %s | log-concave %s | unimodal %s'%(name,n,box,E,E==0,len(iu),viol,n,Fm1,len(lv),lv[0],lv[-1],mx,pk,logc,unim))
    print('   level sizes:',seq)
# constraint graph of Λ9: the seven edges of Λ8 plus g–2S′
edges8={(1,0),(2,1),(3,2),(7,2),(6,3),(5,4),(6,5)}; edges9=edges8|{(8,6)}
def is_tree(nv,edges):
    adj=collections.defaultdict(set)
    for a,b in edges: adj[a].add(b); adj[b].add(a)
    seen={0}; st=[0]
    while st:
        u=st.pop()
        for w in adj[u]:
            if w not in seen: seen.add(w); st.append(w)
    return len(seen)==nv and len(edges)==nv-1
deg9=collections.Counter([a for a,b in edges9]+[b for a,b in edges9])
print('constraint graph Λ9: 9 vertices, %d edges, tree %s | 2S′ (index 8) degree %d (a leaf, attached at g): %s'%(len(edges9),is_tree(9,edges9),deg9[8],deg9[8]==1 and (8,6) in edges9))
# projection Λ9 → Λ8 (drop 2S′): exact; fibre sizes
proj=collections.Counter(tuple(c[:8]) for c in L9); S8=set(L8)
print('projection of Λ9 onto the first eight coordinates: %d cells, equal to Λ8: %s | fibre sizes (preimages per Λ8 cell): min %d, max %d, distribution %s | mean = %d/%d = %.4f'%(len(proj),set(proj)==S8,min(proj.values()),max(proj.values()),dict(sorted(collections.Counter(proj.values()).items())),len(L9),len(L8),len(L9)/len(L8)))
print('   fibre size = g+1 for every cell:',all(proj[c]==c[6]+1 for c in L8))

# READ-ch12d — Phase R2, main volume §12.10 "An axis the index did not carry, and now does" (chat 72)

Member The_Method_1_6-2.md (BUILD90 main, md5 4aef772b…), L2484–L2523 (40 lines; §12.11 opens at L2524), read in full against each cited section, Appendix E (Q) and the Register, the rebuilt tower (tower-2.py, c0bce27a…), the segment instrument r2-ch12d.py (beside tower-2.py; every row of the §12.10.1 table measured on all 1,654 cells and all 1,367,031 unordered pairs of Λ₉) and r2-tools.py. Rulings applied as in READ-ch7. Census rows in range: 1057, 1058 (both C9, the two "never"s of L2489), closed in CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch12d.tsv. Every printed number in the segment reproduces (§B).

## A. Deviations (both texts)

**12d-01 · L2520–2521 (§12.10.2) — "recorded in Q" points at no Q item.** PRINTED: `What remains is a data lookup, recorded in Q: whether the measured target terms of the 153 channels saturate min(g, 4f+2−g).` SOURCE: Appendix E "Q, indexed and closed" (L10898–11200) lists items A, B, C, D, F, G, H, I, K, M, N, O, P, R; the only item touching 2S′ is **O** — `tree propagation retested on Λ₉′'s f–g–2S′ cycle — CLOSED`; item I is `the spectroscopic v-check per channel` (the Λ₁₀ axis v, not 2S′). MEASURED (grep of L10898–11200 for '2S′', 'target', 'saturat', 'min(g', '4f+2', 'spin', 'selection', 'lookup'; of the whole main for 'target term', 'saturate'): no item records this lookup; 'target term' occurs at L2520 only. READING: a pointer to a record that does not exist — the lookup is either unrecorded or was closed without the item; either way the sentence cannot be followed. Class of 11-03 (wrong site) / 12a-01 (no site). Substance for the Q index (Appendix E segment settles whether an item is owed).

**12d-02 · L2496–2509 (§12.10.1 table) — no Register entry for the Λ₉ column beyond its cell count, and one row samples a population that is exhaustively measurable.** PRINTED Λ₉ column: `box 27,648 · E(X) 0 · sublattice yes · rank-modular 200,000 tested, 0 violations · constraint graph a tree — 2S′ attaches as a leaf · F(1) 1,654 · F(−1) 2 · rank levels 21, widest 185 at 12 · log-concave yes`; L2508–2509 `fibres of one to four preimages, mean 1.69`. SOURCE: Register entries with 1,654 → 393, 621, 622, 623, 1011, 1788, 1790 (the count, the composable share 1,169/1,654, the tower-entry correction, the Λ₁₃ constraint graph); '27,648' → none; '185' → 185 (an entry number), 334 (branching "up to 185 ways"), 609 (a tally); '1.69' → 973 (a quantum defect); '2S′ ≤ g' → 444, 621, 623, 626, 1790 (the bound named, no table figure). MEASURED (r2-ch12d.py): box 27,648; E = 0; rank-modularity r(x)+r(y) = r(x∨y)+r(x∧y) on **all 1,367,031 pairs, 0 violations**; 9 vertices, 8 edges, tree, 2S′ a leaf at g; F(1) = 1,654; F(−1) = 2; 21 levels (ranks 3..23), level sizes 1, 5, 15, 35, 63, 98, 131, 159, 177, **185**, 181, 165, 139, 108, 77, 51, 32, 18, 9, 4, 1, widest at rank 12; log-concave and unimodal; projection onto the first eight coordinates = Λ₈ exactly; fibre sizes {1: 485, 2: 320, 3: 155, 4: 16} = g+1 at every cell; mean 1,654/976 = 1.6947. READING: every figure is right and none but 1,654 is in the record — the class of 12c-05. The "200,000 tested" row is moreover a tautology once E = 0 holds: with join and meet coordinatewise and rank the coordinate sum, r(x∨y) + r(x∧y) = Σ(max + min) = r(x) + r(y) identically (INFERRED from the identity; MEASURED on every pair). Provenance; lower.

**12d-03 · layout.** L2487, L2496 (the table's header line), L2517–2521 four-space lines render as code (r2-tools.py layout); the §12.10.2 paragraph that carries the section's substantive update (2S′ ≤ g confirmed by §12.11.1) is set as code. Production.

## B. Verified (all MEASURED unless marked)

- L2485 A_q carries 2S and B_q none: the A side is (n, ℓ, k, 2S), the B side (e, f, g) — r2-ch12b, r2-ch12c.
- L2489 "never a closure defect": E(Λ₈) = 0 on the eight supplied coordinates (r2-ch12c, minmax.py); ℛ acts on supplied coordinates only, so an absent axis is not a closure defect by definition — the two "never"s are definitional (census 1057, 1058: not a defect). "An axis E2 admits" — E2 is defined at §17.2 (L4799 "E2 — which axes may be adjoined"), 2,300 lines later, with no pointer here; incidental.
- L2493–2494 2S ≤ k is §7.1's vector-coupling bound (L1760); 2S′ ≤ g is the same form on the target — tower-2.py L9 implements exactly `2S′ ∈ [0, g]`, and it is the bound Register 621 reproduced 1,654 with. §12.10.2 itself says the bound was built by analogy; consistent.
- L2497–2506 the Λ₈ column reproduces in full (976; 6,912; E = 0; sublattice; 0 violations on 475,800; tree; F(1) = 976; F(−1) = 2; 18 levels, 122 at 11; log-concave) — r2-ch12d agrees with r2-ch8, r2-ch11, r2-ch12c.
- L2508–2509 Λ₈ is the exact projection of Λ₉ (976 cells, identical); fibres 1 to 4 preimages, mean 1.69 (12d-02 for the figures). §31.2.4 (L8685 "No critical dimension, and a ladder") resolves to its heading.
- L2514–2519 "built by analogy and not from spectroscopy … §12.11.1 has since answered it: … zero violations over every fibre … not tight, in the two ways §12.11.2 names": §12.11.1 (L3032) and §12.11.2 (L3363) resolve to their headings; the claims are record-carried to those segments (see also HANDOFF-22's deferred item on the tower amendment at L2406–2408 and Λ₁₀'s 2S′ ≤ v ≤ g; Register 1790 records 2S′ ≤ g at Λ₉ and 2S′ ≤ v ≤ g at Λ₁₀, and the triangle 2S′–g–v from Λ₁₀).
- L2521 "153 channels": Appendix B's channel count (L641, L8189) — consistent; min(g, 4f+2−g) appears at L3093, L3096, L3368 (§12.11.1.x, §12.11.2) — consistent.

## C. Incidental

- §12.10's heading claim ("an axis the index did not carry, and now does") is the book's own account of its history; the tower instrument carries the axis and reproduces every figure.
- r2-ch12d.py prints both stages' level sequences if R3 restates the table with the exhaustive pair count in place of "200,000 tested".

 2536|  **Λ₈'s two ends are not the same shape.** Its source is (n, ℓ, k, 2S) and its target is (e, f, g) —
 2537|  four coordinates against three. A transition's output is therefore not a legal input, and **Λ₈ cannot
 2538|  be iterated**: no cascade, no sequence, no second step. The asymmetry is a missing spin.
 2539| 
 2540|  **The ninth axis supplies it.** 2S′ ≤ g gives the target its own multiplicity, and the target end
 2541|  becomes (e, f, g, 2S′) under exactly the source's constraint forms — f ≤ e−1 against ℓ ≤ n−1,
 2542|  g ≤ 4f+2 against k ≤ 4ℓ+2, 2S′ ≤ g against 2S ≤ k. All 1,654 targets of Λ₉ are legal sources.
 2543| 
 2544|     Define b ∘ a when a's target equals b's source: the composite runs a's source to b's target,
 2545|     transferring min(q_a, q_b) — no more than was taken, no more than arrives.
 2546| 
 2547|  **Λ₉ is closed under composition, exhaustively: 41,682 composable pairs, zero failures**, and
 2548|  associative on 8,434 sampled triples with none. Λ₉ is therefore not merely a lattice of transitions
 2549|  but a **category of them**, and composition is time — not a stamp on a cell but an order between
 2550|  cells.
 2551| 
 2552|  **And Λ₉ is the only stage of the tower that composes.** Composition needs the target's coordinate
 2553|  set to be matched by a source set of the same shape. Every axis above the ninth attaches to one end
 2554|  or to the joint object, and the shapes part company:
 2555| 
 2556|   stage   target                          source                    composes
 2557|   Λ₈      (e, f, g)                       (n, ℓ, k, 2S)             no — 3 against 4
 2558|   **Λ₉**  **(e, f, g, 2S′)**              **(n, ℓ, k, 2S)**         **yes — 41,682 pairs, 0 failures**
 2559|   Λ₁₀     (e, f, g, 2S′, v)               (n, ℓ, k, 2S)             no — no source seniority exists
 2560|   Λ₁₁     (e, f, g, 2S′, v)               (n, ℓ, k, 2S, 2J_c)       no — 2J_c is the source's alone
 2561|   Λ₁₂     K binds core to orbit — joint    —                        no — not an end coordinate
 2562|   Λ₁₃     2J binds K to spin — joint       —                        no
 2563| 
 2564|  **So the tower carries three gradings, not two.** §12.11.3's dichotomy sorts the axes into counting
 2565|  and coupling — exact and envelope. Composability sorts them differently and **more strictly**: it is
 2566|  lost at axis 10, one step before exactness is, because v is a counting coordinate that closes exactly
 2567|  and still has no source counterpart. **An axis can be exact and not composable; none is composable
 2568|  and not exact.** Λ₉ sits alone at the top of the stricter grading, and the tower above it is the
 2569|  record of what each further coordinate costs — first composition, then exactness.

 2572|  advice, for the physics of the target's multiplicity; nothing in that argument mentions composability,

 2575|  what an index defends itself with. Register 313.

# r2-ch12e.py — Phase R2 instrument for main §12.11 and §12.11.0 (chat 72). Requires tower-2.py beside it.
# Composition on Λ9 measured on ALL ordered pairs and ALL composable triples (the print: 41,682 pairs, 8,434 sampled triples).
import importlib.util, collections, itertools
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('tower','tower-2.py'); tw=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(tw)
L8=tw.L8(); L9=tw.L9(); S9=set(L9)
src=lambda c:(c[0],c[1],c[2],c[7]); tgt=lambda c:(c[4],c[5],c[6],c[8])
sources=set(map(src,L9)); targets=set(map(tgt,L9))
print('|Λ9| =',len(L9),'| distinct sources (n,ℓ,k,2S):',len(sources),'| distinct targets (e,f,g,2S′):',len(targets))
legal=[c for c in L9 if tgt(c) in sources]; print('§12.11.0 "all 1,654 targets of Λ9 are legal sources": cells whose target is a source of some cell: %d of %d | targets ∉ sources: %d, all with g = 0: %s (k ≥ 1 in every source; §10.2)'%(len(legal),len(L9),len(L9)-len(legal),all(c[6]==0 for c in L9 if tgt(c) not in sources)))
print('  Λ8 (n,ℓ,k,2S) against (e,f,g): shapes 4 against 3 — no composition defined; source set of Λ8 %d = its A-set'%len({src(c) for c in L8}))
# composition b∘a when tgt(a) == src(b): composite = (src(a), q = min(q_a,q_b), tgt(b))
bysrc=collections.defaultdict(list)
for b in L9: bysrc[src(b)].append(b)
def comp(a,b): return (a[0],a[1],a[2],min(a[3],b[3]),b[4],b[5],b[6],a[7],b[8])
pairs=0; fail=0; qle=0
for a in L9:
    for b in bysrc.get(tgt(a),()):
        pairs+=1; c=comp(a,b)
        if c not in S9: fail+=1
        if b[3]<=a[3]: qle+=1
print('  composable ordered pairs (a,b), target(a) = source(b): %d | composite ∈ Λ9: failures %d | q_b ≤ q_a in every pair (so min(q_a,q_b) = q_b): %s'%(pairs,fail,qle==pairs))
trip=0; afail=0
for a in L9:
    for b in bysrc.get(tgt(a),()):
        for c in bysrc.get(tgt(b),()):
            trip+=1
            if comp(comp(a,b),c)!=comp(a,comp(b,c)): afail+=1
print('  composable triples (a,b,c): %d | (c∘b)∘a ≠ c∘(b∘a): %d (print: 8,434 sampled, none)'%(trip,afail))
# predecessors and successors: cells with at least one predecessor / successor / both (Register 621–623: composable 1,169 of 1,654 = 70.7 %)
has_succ={c for c in L9 if tgt(c) in sources}; bytgt=collections.defaultdict(int)
for a in L9: bytgt[tgt(a)]+=1
has_pred={c for c in L9 if src(c) in targets}
print('  cells with a successor: %d | with a predecessor: %d | with both: %d | with either: %d (of 1,654; Register 621: composable 1,169 = 70.7 %%)'%(len(has_succ),len(has_pred),len(has_succ&has_pred),len(has_succ|has_pred)))
print('  composable cells with g = q (Register 621 "conservative share 739 of 1,169"): %d of %d'%(sum(1 for c in has_succ if c[6]==c[3]),len(has_succ)))
# the table L2556–2562: which end each tower axis attaches to, read from tower-2.py's bounds
print('  tower axes (tower-2.py): 2S′ ∈ [0,g] → target end; v ∈ [2S′,g] → target end; 2Jc ∈ [0,φ̂(k)] → source end; 2K ∈ [0, 2Jc+2·FMAX] → joint (Jc is source, the cap stands for f); 2J ∈ [2K−1, 2K+1] → joint')
for d in (10,11):
    L=tw.STAGES[d](); ends=len({(c[4],c[5],c[6],c[8],c[9]) for c in L}); print('  Λ%d: target set (e,f,g,2S′,v) has %d members, source set %s %d members — no target is a source (shapes differ): composition undefined'%(d,ends,'(n,ℓ,k,2S)' if d==10 else '(n,ℓ,k,2S,2Jc)',len({src(c) for c in L}) if d==10 else len({(c[0],c[1],c[2],c[7],c[10]) for c in L})))
# Figure 12.4 caption: "the forbidden f···K bridge … priced at 3.5%" — §12.11.1 L3067: 2K ≤ 2Jc + 2f (the cell's f) instead of 2Jc + 2·FMAX
L11=tw.L11(); L12=tw.L12()
L12f=[c+(K2,) for c in L11 for K2 in range(0, c[10]+2*c[5]+1)]
A12=lambda c:(c[0],c[1],c[2],c[7],c[10],c[11]); B12=lambda c:(c[4],c[5],c[6],c[8],c[9])
def sep(L):
    tot=0
    for qq in range(4):
        C=[c for c in L if c[3]==qq]; tot+=len({A12(c) for c in C})*len({B12(c) for c in C})
    return tot
print('  Λ12 with the cap (2K ≤ 2Jc + 2): %d cells, Σ_q|A(q)||B(q)| = %d (exact: %s) | with the cell\'s f (2K ≤ 2Jc + 2f): %d cells, Σ_q|A(q)||B(q)| = %d, over-count %.2f %% (L3067 "breaks the factorisation by 3.5%%")'%(len(L12),sep(L12),sep(L12)==len(L12),len(L12f),sep(L12f),100*(sep(L12f)-len(L12f))/len(L12f)))
# the tower's constraint graph: 13 nodes; edges from every two-coordinate bound (tower-2.py), with and without Λ9's 2S′ ≤ g once Λ10's 2S′ ≤ v ≤ g is present
E8={(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(2,7),(3,6),(4,5),(5,6)}; E13=E8|{(6,8),(8,9),(6,9),(2,10),(10,11),(11,12)}
def cyc(nv,E):
    adj=collections.defaultdict(set)
    for a,b in E: adj[a].add(b); adj[b].add(a)
    seen={0}; st=[0]
    while st:
        u=st.pop()
        for w in adj[u]:
            if w not in seen: seen.add(w); st.append(w)
    return len(E)-nv+1 if len(seen)==nv else None
print('  Λ13 constraint graph with every bound drawn: 13 nodes, %d edges, cycle rank %s (the triangle 2S′–g–v; Register 1790) | with 2S′ ≤ g omitted as implied by 2S′ ≤ v ≤ g: %d edges, cycle rank %s — a tree (Figure 12.4 caption, the L2406–2408 amendment)'%(len(E13),cyc(13,E13),len(E13)-1,cyc(13,E13-{(6,8)})))

# READ-ch12e — Phase R2, main volume §12.11 "The tower — Λ₉ to Λ₁₃" (head) and §12.11.0 "Transitions compose" (chat 72)

Member The_Method_1_6-2.md (BUILD90 main, md5 4aef772b…), L2524–L2576 (53 lines; §12.11.0.1 opens at L2577), read in full against each cited section, the MC entry "Transitions compose" (MC L1232–1238) and the Register (313, 621–623, 1790), the rebuilt tower (tower-2.py, c0bce27a…), the segment instrument r2-ch12e.py (beside tower-2.py; composition measured on all 1,654 × 1,654 ordered pairs and all composable triples of Λ₉) and r2-tools.py. Rulings applied as in READ-ch7. Census rows in range: none; CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch12e.tsv is the header alone.

## A. Deviations (both texts)

**12e-01 · L2542 (§12.11.0), and MC L1234 — "all 1,654 targets of Λ₉ are legal sources" is false for 485 cells.** PRINTED L2540–2542: `2S′ ≤ g gives the target its own multiplicity, and the target end becomes (e, f, g, 2S′) under exactly the source's constraint forms … All 1,654 targets of Λ₉ are legal sources.` MC L1234: `makes all 1,654 targets of Λ₉ legal sources`. SOURCE: every source has k ≥ 1 (§10.2's eighth condition; r2-ch10: 25 cells with k = 0 excluded), while a target may have g = 0. Register 622: `Λ₉ 1,654 and 1,169` composable; 621: `the reachable fraction … 1,169 of 1,654 = 70.7%`. MEASURED (r2-ch12e.py): distinct sources 33, distinct targets 38; cells whose target is a source **1,169 of 1,654**; the 485 others all have g = 0, and no source has k = 0. READING: the sentence asserts for every cell what holds for 70.7 % of them, and contradicts the Register's own count two paragraphs before the count is used (41,682 pairs is the count over the 1,169). The forms match (f ≤ e−1 / ℓ ≤ n−1, g ≤ 4f+2 / k ≤ 4ℓ+2, 2S′ ≤ g / 2S ≤ k); the caps do not (k ≥ 1 against g ≥ 0). Substance (an "all" false in general; class of 9-02, 11-01, 12c-02). For R3: "every target with g ≥ 1 is a legal source — 1,169 of 1,654".

**12e-02 · L2548 against MC L1236 — the main prints a sample where its compendium holds the population.** PRINTED L2547–2548: `41,682 composable pairs, zero failures, and associative on 8,434 sampled triples with none`. MC L1236: `associativity over all 842,206 composable triples`. MEASURED: composable ordered pairs 41,682, composites in Λ₉ with 0 failures; composable triples **842,206**, associativity failures 0. READING: agreement; the main should carry the population figure its MC entry has (class of 12c-06). No Register entry carries either count (Register 313 records the finding — `Λ₉ composes, and is a category` — without a number; '41,682' and '8,434' have no Register site); provenance, as 12c-05.

**12e-03 · L2040 (Chapter 10, deferred here) — "Λ₉ has both [a predecessor and a successor]" is true of the index and not of every cell.** PRINTED L2039–2040: `what a transition can have is a predecessor and a successor, and §12.11.0 shows Λ₉ has both.` MEASURED: every one of the 1,654 cells has a predecessor (the 33 sources are all among the 38 targets); 1,169 have a successor; 485 have none. READING: as a statement about the index, true; as read against 12e-01's "all", a reader takes every cell to have both. Lower, wording; the Chapter 10 deferred item closes on this measurement.

**12e-04 · Figure 12.4 caption L2531–2533 — "constraint tree of the full tower" and "priced at 3.5%" both rest on §12.11.1's conventions, and the record disagrees with the first.** PRINTED: `The constraint tree of the full tower: two caterpillars glued at k–q … with the forbidden f···K bridge dashed and priced at 3.5%.` SOURCE: the §12.7.1 amendment L2406–2408 (`two caterpillars glued spine to spine at k–q — A runs n–ℓ–k–J_c–K–J with 2S pendant, B runs e–f–g–v–2S′`); L3065–3067 (`2K ≤ 2J_c + 2f_max has one parent and preserves the tree … the same bound written with the cell's f has two parents and breaks the factorisation by 3.5%`); Register 1790: `Λ₁₃'S CONSTRAINT GRAPH IS 13 NODES AND 14 EDGES WITH ONE TRIANGLE, 2S′–g–v, FROM Λ₁₀ ONWARD`. MEASURED (r2-ch12e.py, tower-2.py's bounds): with every bound drawn, 13 nodes and 13 edges, cycle rank 1 (the triangle 2S′–g–v; the instrument has no f–K edge, its 2K bound uses the cap); with 2S′ ≤ g omitted as implied by Λ₁₀'s 2S′ ≤ v ≤ g, 12 edges, cycle rank 0 — the caption's tree. Under the literal reading of L3067 (2K ≤ 2J_c + 2f, the cell's f) the stage has 55,755 cells against Σ_q|A(q)||B(q)| = 70,905 — an over-count of 27.17 % (21.37 % of the product), **not 3.5 %**. READING: the caption's "tree" is the amendment's drawing (the implied edge dropped) and contradicts Register 1790's measured graph (the edge counted); which convention the book adopts is the deferred §12.11.1 item and is not settled here. The 3.5 % is not reproduced under the literal reading; the computation §12.11.5 means is to be read there before any finding (G0v). Carried to §12.11.1 / §12.11.5.

**12e-05 · L2567–2568 against §12.10.2 L2519 — "none is composable and not exact" needs axis 9 to be exact, and §12.10.2 says its bound is not tight.** PRINTED L2564–2568: `§12.11.3's dichotomy sorts the axes into counting and coupling — exact and envelope … composability … is lost at axis 10, one step before exactness is … An axis can be exact and not composable; none is composable and not exact.` L2519 (§12.10.2): `exact vector coupling confirms 2S′ ≤ g as a true bound — zero violations over every fibre — and shows it is not tight, in the two ways §12.11.2 names.` READING: the only composable axis is the ninth; the sentence classes it exact, while §12.10.2 classes its bound as containing but not tight (an envelope in Chapter 7's sense, L1746). Whether §12.11.3 files axis 9 as exact or envelope decides which sentence is wrong — record-carried to the §12.11.3 segment (L3394–3456), not resolved here. Lower until read.

**12e-06 · layout.** L2544–2545 four-space lines render as code; the L2556–2562 stage table is a column-dump (three-gap alignment, not a table). Production.

## B. Verified (all MEASURED unless marked)

- L2536–2538 Λ₈'s source (n, ℓ, k, 2S) and target (e, f, g): four against three; no composition is defined; the source set is the 33-element A-set (r2-ch12c).
- L2544–2545 the composite b ∘ a = (source a, min(q_a, q_b), target b): in every one of the 41,682 composable pairs q_b ≤ q_a (target(a) = source(b) gives q_b ≤ k_b = g_a ≤ q_a), so the transfer is always q_b — the min is never the smaller argument on the left; incidental. Closure: 0 composites outside Λ₉ — also immediate from the constraint forms (INFERRED: q_b ≤ k_a, g_b ≤ q_b, 2S_a ≤ k_a, 2S′_b ≤ g_b).
- L2547–2549 category: identities are not discussed in the print; associativity exhaustive (842,206 triples) — the MC's figure; "composition is time — an order between cells" is the book's reading, not a measurement.
- L2556–2562 the stage table: tower-2.py attaches 2S′ ∈ [0, g] and v ∈ [2S′, g] to the target end, 2J_c ∈ [0, φ̂(k)] to the source end, 2K and 2J to the joint object; at Λ₁₀ the 70 target tuples (e, f, g, 2S′, v) and 33 source tuples (n, ℓ, k, 2S) share none, at Λ₁₁ the 70 targets and 163 sources (n, ℓ, k, 2S, 2J_c) share none — composition undefined above Λ₉, as printed. INFERRED for Λ₁₂–Λ₁₃ ("joint"), from the bounds.
- L2571–2575 §12.11.1 (L3032) and Chapter 16 (L4332) resolve to their headings; Register 313 (R L1163) resolves to its headline, which is this section's claim (`Λ₉ composes, and is a category`); "the ninth axis was added for seniority" — seniority is Λ₁₀'s v in the tower table (L2559 "no source seniority exists"); the sentence says 2S′ was taken "for the physics of the target's multiplicity" — the heading's "for seniority" is loose; incidental.
- L2526 §12.10 resolves; L2532 "the Chapter 7 dichotomy" resolves to Chapter 7 (L1724; the counting/coupling split at L1745–1748).
- Register 621's composable share 739 of 1,169 (g = q) reproduces; every cell has a predecessor, 1,169 a successor.
- Figure 12.4 placed at L2529; no second main site of "Figure 12.4"; its file is not a bundle member — production check.

## C. Incidental

- HANDOFF-22's deferred items for this segment: "41,682 pairs, associative" — closed, exhaustive (12e-02); "Λ₉ has a predecessor and a successor" (L2040, L2143) — closed (12e-03; L2143 states only "closed under composition", which holds).
- Added to the §12.11.1 / §12.11.5 deferral: L3067's "3.5 %" (12e-04) and the axis-9 exact/envelope classification (12e-05, §12.11.3).
- r2-ch12e.py prints the source/target sets at every stage and the f-bridge counts if R3 restates L2542 or the caption.

OLD='The_Method_1_6_BUILD97_compendia_papers_audits.md'; NEW='The_Method_1_6_BUILD98_compendia_papers_audits.md'
assert not os.path.exists(NEW)
old=open(OLD,encoding='utf-8').read(); assert hashlib.md5(old.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()=='3446dafd21514258ed9a25d2f9c08d17'
pat=re.compile(r'^<<<FILE: (.+?)>>>\n(.*?)<<<END FILE: \1>>>', re.S|re.M)
names=[m.group(1) for m in pat.finditer(old)]; assert len(names)==166 and len(set(names))==166
new_members=['READ-ch12c.md','CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch12c.tsv','r2-ch12c.py','READ-ch12d.md','CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch12d.tsv','r2-ch12d.py','READ-ch12e.md','CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch12e.tsv','r2-ch12e.py']
assert not (set(new_members)&set(names)), 'member-name collision'
# 1. replace the WORKING-REGISTER.md member body with the W-108 version (append-only within the member)
wr_old=[m for m in pat.finditer(old) if m.group(1)=='WORKING-REGISTER.md']; assert len(wr_old)==1; m=wr_old[0]
wr_new=open('members/WORKING-REGISTER.md',encoding='utf-8').read(); assert wr_new.startswith(m.group(2)) and len(wr_new)>len(m.group(2))
txt=old[:m.start(2)]+wr_new+old[m.end(2):]
# 2. append the nine members after the last END marker
last=old.rfind('<<<END FILE: '); endpos=old.find('>>>',last)+3; tail=old[endpos:]; print('tail after last END marker:',repr(tail))
add=''.join('\n<<<FILE: %s>>>\n%s<<<END FILE: %s>>>\n'%(n,open('members/'+n,encoding='utf-8').read(),n) for n in new_members)
txt=txt.rstrip('\n')+'\n'+add if not tail.endswith('\n') else txt+add

newtxt=b.decode('utf-8'); ms=pat.findall(newtxt); print('members',len(ms),'unique',len(set(n for n,_ in ms)))
changed=[n for n,body in ms if n in names and body!=dict(pat.findall(old))[n]]; print('old members changed:',changed)
for n,body in ms:

rev=newtxt.replace(add,'',1); rev=rev.replace(wr_new, m.group(2),1)

# 5. diff: additions only
import difflib
o=old.split('\n'); nn=newtxt.split('\n'); sm=difflib.SequenceMatcher(None,o,nn,autojunk=False)
plus=sum(j2-j1 for tag,i1,i2,j1,j2 in sm.get_opcodes() if tag=='insert'); minus=sum(i2-i1 for tag,i1,i2,j1,j2 in sm.get_opcodes() if tag in('delete','replace')); rep=sum(j2-j1 for tag,i1,i2,j1,j2 in sm.get_opcodes() if tag=='replace')
